name: Reconciliation
desc: Two people who stopped speaking, sitting down again. No apology is spoken.

sets.place: front porch, late afternoon, wooden steps, open door, long shadows, outdoors

shots.desc: a front porch in late afternoon, two wooden chairs side by side, one door standing open, long shadows across the boards, no humans, wide shot
standing at the foot of the porch steps, hands at sides, looking up toward the open door, full body, wide shot
eyes lifting to meet another, brow softening, small nod, close-up
a second cup set down on a porch rail beside the first, steam rising, close-up, no humans
two empty chairs on a porch turned to face the same garden, long shadows, no humans, wide shot

why: For the scene where the apology is not the point and would ruin it if spoken. There is no speak shot here, for a craft reason and a mechanical one. The craft reason is that a reconciliation played in dialogue almost always overstates itself. The mechanical one is that resolve - the only emotion in the library reading as calm certainty - has the mouth tag 'closed mouth', which sits earlier in the prompt than any shot desc and would shut the mouth of a talking shot anyway. So the reconciliation is carried by objects and one look: a second cup appearing beside the first, and two chairs facing the same way. The cue is silence, which drops all score - its own card calls it the most under-used cue in the library, and it is right here, because a warm string cue would tell the audience how to feel about something the images are already doing. warm_memory was the obvious pick and is wrong: its own note says a major key against a minor-key film reads as 'then', not 'now', and this scene has to be happening now. Every shot holds exactly one person or none - no framing asks for two people at once, because character cards carry the tag 'solo' near the front of the prompt and it beats any later request for a second figure.
note: Shots, the golden grade, pace, camera and wear render today. Not working: (1) transition 'dissolve' is recorded but short.py cuts hard on every boundary. (2) emotion 'resolve' is status:partial - voice_style 'steady' is not routed to TTS, which costs nothing here because nobody speaks. One thing to watch: resolve's body tag is 'upright, still' and it applies at wear 0, so this template deliberately never asks anyone to sit down on camera - the sitting-together image is delivered by the peopleless pillow shot of two chairs instead. At wear 0 the fallback WEAR list appends 'clean uniform, neat hair' to shots 2 and 3 - give these characters a wear_tags override or they will reconcile in uniform.
